title: Your first image: checkpoint, sampler, VAE

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the compression factor between the original image elements and the latent elements for a 64x64 image?
questions.why: The lesson explicitly calculates the compression factor as Image Elements (12,288) divided by Latent Elements (256), which equals 48.

questions.q: In the context of ComfyUI's architecture, which class is responsible for executing the denoising loop and applying conditioning?
questions.why: The section 'In ComfyUI' states that 'The KSAMPLER class in comfy/samplers.py executes the denoising loop.'

questions.q: What are the three components contained within a Checkpoint file, as described in the 'intuition' section?
questions.answer: The UNet (engine), CLIP text encoders (navigation charts), and the VAE (hull plating).
questions.why: The lesson states: 'The Checkpoint is your ship. It contains the engine (the UNet), the navigation charts (CLIP text encoders), and the hull plating (the VAE).'

questions.q: What is the shape of the text embedding tensor (`text_emb`) used in the lab simulation?
questions.why: The 'Under the hood' section and the 'Lab' section both specify that the text embedding tensor has a shape of `(1, 77, 768)`.

questions.q: Why is working in latent space computationally feasible for diffusion models, according to the lesson?
questions.answer: Because the VAE compresses the data, allowing the model to work with significantly fewer numbers (e.g., 256 latent elements vs. 12,288 image elements) than the final image.
questions.why: The lesson states: 'We are working with 48 times fewer numbers than the final image. This is why diffusion models are computationally feasible.'
